sentences.text: The concurrent verdicts of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Perambra and the Additional Sessions Court Fast Track (Adhoc)-II, Kozhikode in C.C No.5/2001 and Crl.A No.498/2004 respectively, convicting and sentencing the petitioner for the commission of offence under Section 498A I.P.C are under challenge in this revision petition.

sentences.text:
2. The aforesaid case arose out of the final report filed by the S.H.O of Police, Meppayur in Crime No.73/2000 alleging the commission of offence under Sections 406 and 498A r/w Section 34 I.P.C,
against the petitioner herein and two others.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: The allegation in the aforesaid case was that the petitioner, who married PW1 on 28.12.1998, had been subjecting PW1 to matrimonial cruelty, along with the other accused, who are his close relatives.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text:
It was further alleged that the petitioner and the other accused misappropriated the entire gold ornaments of PW1.
3.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: In the trial before the learned Magistrate, the prosecution examined four witnesses as PW1 to PW4, and brought on record two documents as Exts.P1 and P2.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: After analysing the aforesaid evidence, 2026:KER:29983 Crl.R.P No.3859/2006    3 the learned Magistrate found that the offence under Section 406 I.P.C is not brought out, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: It was further held that the prosecution has not succeeded in establishing the offences alleged against accused Nos.2 and 3.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text:
However, the petitioner/first accused was found guilty of Section 498A I.P.C,
and convicted thereunder.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: He was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for two months and fine Rs.2,000/- with a default clause of simple imprisonment for fifteen days for the commission of the aforesaid offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: Though the petitioner challenged the aforesaid verdict in appeal, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, who considered the appeal, found no reasons to interfere with the findings of the learned Magistrate.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appeal was dismissed, confirming the findings of the Trial Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the above concurrent verdicts of the Courts below, the petitioner is here before this Court with this revision petition.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text:
4. Since there was no representation on the part of the petitioner, notice was issued to him,
intimating the adjournment of the case and also informing him that the case would be decided in his absence, if there was no representation on the adjourned posting date.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: The aforesaid notice to the revision petitioner was returned with the 2026:KER:29983 Crl.R.P No.3859/2006    4 endorsement 'not known'.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, Adv.Sruthy.K.K was appointed as Amicus Curiae to represent the revision petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: 5. Heard both sides.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text:
6. The Trial Court mainly relied on the evidence tendered by the victim of the offence as PW1, to arrive at the conclusion that the prosecution has successfully established the commission of offence Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131541715/
2 under Section 498A I.P.C by the petitioner herein.

sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: In addition to the aforesaid evidence, the Trial Court placed reliance on the evidence of PW2 and PW3, which corroborated the evidence tendered by PW1 about the cruelty meted out to her at the hands of the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text:
The aforesaid evidence of PW1 to PW3 brought out the persistent acts of cruelty meted out to PW1 by the petitioner herein,
right from the early days of his marriage with her.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: The learned Magistrate observed that the mental cruelty inflicted by the petitioner even extended to such an intolerable level of denying the paternity of the twin children born to PW1 in the wedlock with the petitioner, and attempting to inflict bodily harm to those children.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: The Appellate Court made a re-appraisal of the aforesaid evidence, and held that the findings of the learned Magistrate are not liable to be interfered with, in appeal.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: Having regard to the 2026:KER:29983 Crl.R.P No.3859/2006    5 aforesaid concurrent findings on facts of the Courts below, I am of the view that there is absolutely no scope for dislodging the conclusions of the Courts below about the commission of offence under Section 498A I.P.C by the petitioner herein, in exercise of the revisional powers of this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: As regards the sentence portion
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text:
,
it is seen that a balanced and reasonable punishment has been awarded by the Trial Court, and it has been upheld by the Appellate Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: Having regard to the nature and gravity of the offence involved in this case, it cannot be said that the sentence of simple imprisonment for two months and fine Rs.2,000/- awarded by the Courts below, is excessive or disproportionate.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: Therefore, it has to be concluded that the concurrent verdicts of the Courts below convicting and sentencing the petitioner for the commission of offence under Section 498A I.P.C, are not liable to be interfered in this revision proceedings.
sentences._hearing_file: Gireesh Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 6 April, 2026.json

sentences.text: In the result, the revision petition is hereby dismissed.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
The allegation in the aforesaid case was that the petitioner, who married PW1 on 28.12.1998, had been subjecting PW1 to matrimonial cruelty, along with the other accused, who are his close relatives.
It was further held that the prosecution has not succeeded in establishing the offences alleged against accused Nos.2 and 3.
However, the petitioner/first accused was found guilty of Section 498A I.P.C,
and convicted thereunder.
He was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for two months and fine Rs.2,000/- with a default clause of simple imprisonment for fifteen days for the commission of the aforesaid offence.
In addition to the aforesaid evidence, the Trial Court placed reliance on the evidence of PW2 and PW3, which corroborated the evidence tendered by PW1 about the cruelty meted out to her at the hands of the petitioner.
The Appellate Court made a re-appraisal of the aforesaid evidence, and held that the findings of the learned Magistrate are not liable to be interfered with, in appeal.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
,
it is seen that a balanced and reasonable punishment has been awarded by the Trial Court, and it has been upheld by the Appellate Court.
Having regard to the nature and gravity of the offence involved in this case, it cannot be said that the sentence of simple imprisonment for two months and fine Rs.2,000/- awarded by the Courts below, is excessive or disproportionate.
Therefore, it has to be concluded that the concurrent verdicts of the Courts below convicting and sentencing the petitioner for the commission of offence under Section 498A I.P.C, are not liable to be interfered in this revision proceedings.
opennyai_summary.final__decision: In the result, the revision petition is hereby dismissed.
